prompt: Write one video-generation prompt based on the context. Include a clear subject, setting, visible motion, camera motion, lighting, color palette, and mood. Use concrete image details instead of hype words. Length: 70-130 words. One paragraph only. Do not mention platforms, algorithms, virality, or safety.
Write one caption in ALL CAPS. Length: 3-8 words. Use plain active language about what is visibly happening. End with a period. Return only the caption.

Return one lowercase .mp4 filename, 60 characters or fewer. Use words from the actual subject and motion. Separate words with underscores or hyphens. No dates, camera codes, hashtags, platform names, or filler adjectives.

Write one title, 45-70 characters. Start with the main subject. Add one truthful detail about the motion, reveal, loop, or atmosphere. No clickbait, emojis, ALL-CAPS shouting, brackets, or platform references.

Write a ready-to-post description under 700 characters. Line 1: a direct subject hook plus one gentle action if useful. Body: 1 short paragraph describing what viewers see, including one specific visual change or moment. Final line: 2-3 relevant hashtags. No links unless the context explicitly contains one.

Return 7-10 comma-separated tags. Mix broad category terms with specific subject, style, motion, and loop terms from the context. No leading #, unrelated trends, shock terms, or misspellings unless the context itself uses them.
Return one 2-4 word cover phrase. Make it readable on mobile and tied to the visible subject, motion, loop, or reveal. No hashtags, emojis, platform names, or generic commands.

Write one pinned comment in 1-2 sentences. Ask a specific, answerable question about a visible detail or moment. Avoid sales language and stacked calls to action. No emojis unless the context strongly supports one.
Write one sentence under 120 characters that asks for exactly one action: comment, follow, save, or share. Make it specific to the clip. No emojis and no stacked CTAs.
